title: No Two People Age in the Same Way - Nautilus
gist: A new Science study led by King's College London tracked 335 healthy UK women for eight years and found that aging is highly individualized at the molecular level, with different people showing different patterns of gene-expression and metabolite change over time.

insights.claim: A comprehensive new study published in Science finds that the individuality of human aging is especially pronounced at the molecular level, meaning different people's bodies break down via different biological pathways even when starting from similar baseline health.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Undercuts one-size-fits-all anti-aging interventions and supports a personalized-medicine/biomarker approach to aging diagnostics and longevity products.
insights.quote: the individuality of aging is especially conspicuous at the molecular level.

insights.claim: An international team led by researchers at King's College London followed 335 healthy women from the UK for eight years, taking blood samples to measure expression changes across 16,000 genes as well as levels of hundreds of metabolites.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A concrete, well-powered longitudinal dataset (8 years, 335 subjects, 16,000 genes) that could underpin future aging-biomarker or longevity-diagnostic products.
